title: Management API (/v0/management full surface) — golden recording request
baseline_state: Fresh container from oracle-runner-2's derived S5 baseline config (fleet template from _cpa_edge_ref/run/config.yaml with base-urls re-pointed to the 19999-20007 mock ports and server port 8387) (all 8 mock providers wired, api-keys [oracle-local-key-1], usage-statistics-enabled false, request-retry 0, transient-error-cooldown-seconds -1, logging-to-file absent=false, secret-key bcrypt-hashed in file; management key plaintext oracle-mgmt-key-1). No mock traffic driven through the gateway before the usage/telemetry case so counters are zero. Each case is self-contained and restores its own state; run stateful cases on a freshly started container or after restoring run/config.yaml.

conventions.management_key: Management key literal 'oracle-mgmt-key-1' is the oracle env value documented in reports/oracle/BOOTSTRAP.md §3 (not a real secret). Use it verbatim in recordings. Both header styles are exercised: Authorization: Bearer and X-Management-Key.

conventions.port_substitution: Case bodies below are drafted against the oracle-runner-2 stack (base_url 127.0.0.1:8387; mocks 19999 openai, 20001 gemini, 20002 claude, 20003 codex, 20004 xai, 20005 meta, 20006 interactions, 20007 vertex). The assigned recording worker oracle-runner-4 executes them with the mechanical port map 8387->8407, 19999->21999, 20001->22001, 20002->22002, 20003->22003, 20004->22004, 20005->22005, 20006->22006, 20007->22007. Port numbers anywhere in a transcript are masked dynamic fields for contract replay; everything else is compared byte-exactly.

fixture_deferred.reason: CREDENTIALED-ONLY per BOOTSTRAP §5: completing a vendor OAuth flow requires real vendor accounts (Anthropic/OpenAI/Google/xAI/Devin/Meta). The auth-url response itself (200 {"status":"ok","url":"<vendor authorize URL>","state":"<random>"}) is also per-request random (PKCE + state), so no byte-deterministic golden exists. Error envelopes of the sibling endpoints ARE recorded in S5-oauth-session. Success shape is specified in spec/sections/S5-management-api.md §2.3/§3.6 from upstream source (internal/api/handlers/management/auth_files_provider_oauth.go, oauth_callback.go, oauth_sessions.go).

ForceRefreshAuth performs real vendor token refresh over the network for file-backed OAuth credentials; no local mock exists for vendor auth servers. The validation errors (400 name or all=true is required; 404 auth file not found) are recorded in S5-auth-files-errors. Success shape {"ok":true,"auth":{...}} / {"ok":true,"results":[...]} is specified from upstream source (auth_files_refresh.go).

The endpoint queries the live GitHub releases API (api.github.com/repos/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/releases/latest); the response changes with every upstream release, so no stable golden exists. Shape {"latest-version":"<tag>"} and the 500/502 error shapes are specified from upstream source (config_basic.go GetLatestVersion).

The plugin store reaches an external plugin registry (GitHub-based) whose content changes over time; with plugins disabled in the oracle env the success paths also cannot be exercised. Local no-plugin envelopes are recorded in S5-plugins-list. Shapes specified from upstream source (plugin_store.go, plugins.go, plugin_quota.go).

These require logging-to-file:true plus a populated rotating log directory whose bytes are timestamps of the recording run; a byte-deterministic golden would need a seeded log dir fixture. The disabled-state envelopes are recorded in S5-logs-disabled. Success shapes are specified from upstream source (logs.go). OPTIONAL follow-up: the oracle may seed a deterministic log dir and record this later.
